notes: A weak submission: accepts the 'seasonality + new sales team' red herring, computes revenue growth from a fan-out join (invoice_lines joined to shipments without dedup) so the headline metric is out of tolerance, no cutoff test, generic recommendation. The harness overwrites `metrics` with values deliberately outside tolerance (e.g. expected * 1.35) before grading.

submission.memo_markdown:
Revenue growth of 31% in Q4 looks strong and is consistent with the new enterprise sales team ramping and normal Q4 seasonality. Gross margin is stable so there is no sign of pricing pressure.

We looked at total invoiced amounts by quarter and the trend is up and to the right. Some customers have higher balances than usual but that is expected with larger enterprise deals.

Recommendation: continue investing in the sales team and improve collections processes so that cash catches up with bookings. We should also consider a more conservative returns policy.

Risks: macro conditions could slow enterprise purchasing.

sql_evidence.name: revenue_by_quarter
sql_evidence.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', i.issued_at) AS q, SUM(il.amount_cents) AS revenue
FROM invoices i
JOIN invoice_lines il ON il.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
JOIN shipments s ON s.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

evidence: JOIN shipments s ON s.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
gaps: joins invoice_lines to shipments without deduplication, multiplying revenue by shipment count
no period cutoff test on ship_date vs issued_at

evidence: consistent with the new enterprise sales team ramping and normal Q4 seasonality
gaps: accepts the seasonality/sales-team red herring as the cause
does not examine returns reversals in the following period
does not examine terms_days change on late-quarter invoices

evidence: Revenue growth of 31% in Q4 looks strong
gaps: no explicit answer to the board's question

evidence: macro conditions could slow enterprise purchasing
